steps.title: Electrolytes & acid-base
steps.body: Check K⁺, Na⁺, HCO₃⁻, BUN, and creatinine q6h until stable, then daily. CRRT shifts electrolytes rapidly — especially with citrate and customized replacement fluids.
steps.tip: Hypophosphatemia and hypokalemia are common with aggressive CRRT.

steps.title: Citrate anticoagulation monitoring
steps.body: With regional citrate: ionized Ca²⁺ q4h, total vs ionized calcium ratio, and circuit ionized Ca target per protocol.
steps.tip: Systemic hypocalcemia and metabolic alkalosis are key citrate complications.

steps.title: Circuit checks q2–8h
steps.body: Inspect pressures, air trap, access patency, and effluent line q2h. Full circuit inspection and clot assessment q8h.
steps.tip: Document TMP trend — rising TMP is the earliest clot warning.

steps.title: Clinical assessment q6h
steps.body: Hemodynamics, volume status, daily weight, medication review (especially antibiotics and sedatives cleared by CRRT).
steps.tip: Use NephroGuide CRRT for live dose trends and exportable monitoring plans.
